configClearConfirmMessage: Syncing with this backend stops. Diaries on this device are untouched.
notConfiguredTap: Not configured — tap to set up
stopSubtitle: Syncing in the background — tap to stop
willStop: Will stop once the current item finishes
lanSendSubtitle: Send entries to a device on the same Wi-Fi
lanReceiveSubtitle: Wait for another device to send to this one
autoSyncSubtitle: Push after an entry changes, and pull other devices' changes on a timer
pollIntervalSubtitle: How often to pull other devices' changes in the background
pollIntervalNote: How often a full two-way sync runs in the background. A shorter interval picks up other devices' changes sooner, but every poll takes the remote lock, reads the manifest and makes network requests — too short and you pay for it in traffic and battery, and may hit WebDAV / S3 rate limits or a temporary ban. 30 seconds is a sensible floor.
concurrencySubtitle: Upper bound on parallel network requests while syncing; lower it on a weak connection or against a rate-limited server
concurrencyNote: 8 by default. Higher is faster, but may trip WebDAV / S3 rate limits or get connections refused.
logClearMessage: This deletes the in-memory event stream and every daily jsonl file. It cannot be undone.
logEmpty: No sync events on this date
statusNoBackendDetail: Set one up under Backup and sync
lanSendIntro: Only what the other device is missing gets sent. Changes merge by last-modified time, so sending twice never duplicates anything.
lanAddressHint: Filled in when you pick a device above
lanPinHint: The 6 digits shown on the receiving device
lanPickDevice: Pick a device to send to first
lanSearching: Searching — open the Receive page on the other device
lanApplying: Waiting for the other device to save…
lanPinHelp: Enter it on the sending device · tap to copy
lanUpToDate: Already up to date — nothing changed
lanWaiting: Waiting for the sender to connect…
lanDoneHint: You can keep receiving — the pairing code stays the same
lanFailedHint: The pairing code is unchanged, so the sender can just retry
lanNoWifi: Not on Wi-Fi — this device has no address to show
keyGuardMissing: The remote data is encrypted but its key file (keys.json) is missing, so it cannot be decrypted. Clear the remote data and upload again.
keyGuardMessageMismatch: This device's key cannot decrypt the remote data. Enter the same encryption password as the original device; syncing starts once it checks out.
keyGuardMessage: The remote data is encrypted. Enter the same encryption password as the original device; syncing starts once it checks out.
keyGuardWrong: Wrong password — the remote data cannot be decrypted
keyMismatch: The two passwords do not match
keyChanged: Password changed — the data key is unchanged, so nothing needs re-encrypting
keyEncryptCloudTitle: Encrypt the data already in the cloud
keyEncryptCloudMessage: This backend already holds data. Confirming generates a random data key and encrypts the remote entries, categories and media files. The key itself is wrapped with your password and stored remotely.
keyWriteFailed: Could not write the key file to the cloud, cancelled: {error}
keyDecryptMessage: Turning encryption off decrypts the remote entries, categories and media files back to plain text and deletes the key file. Continue?
keyRemoteEmpty: The remote is empty — only the local key was saved
lanReceiveHint: The sender usually finds this device on its own; the address above can also be typed in by hand. Keep this page open while receiving.
